tool_input.command:
git -C <repo> commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
docs(doctor): DES-077 states the no-Windows-CI gap as a standing fact

The gap was previously a footnote to the exec-bit regression. It is the
common cause of all three Windows defects on this PR, so it is now a
standing statement at the head of the follow-up section, with the two
test-portability findings recorded alongside the exec-bit one.

Verified the CI claim rather than asserting it, and it was not what I
first wrote. Every workflow runs ubuntu-latest with one exception:
test.yml's "verify make tools" matrix adds macos-latest, and that leg
runs `make tools` only, never the Go test suite. So "CI is Linux only"
was wrong as a blanket statement — the tests run on Linux and nowhere
else, and no runner is Windows at all. The text now says exactly that.

Also states the consequence plainly: every Windows guard in this package
is verified by construction — a sandboxGOOS/runtime.GOOS override, a
build tag, or a citation of Go's own Windows source — never by
observation. Any Windows claim in this file is derived from the standard
library's source, not measured.

Adding a Windows CI job is deliberately not proposed here; it is a
separate change with its own cost.
EOF
)" -- DESIGN.md
